claims.text: A CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy coating can adhere to a Cu matrix.
A CrMnFeCoNi coating enhances the wear resistance of a Cu matrix.
The proposed coating is 100 micrometers thick.
The coating is deposited by magnetron sputtering at a substrate temperature of 200°C.
Deposition of the CrMnFeCoNi coating forms a stable oxide layer at the interface between the Cu matrix and the coating.
The stable oxide layer prevents metal-to-metal contact.
Prevention of metal-to-metal contact reduces adhesive wear.
The CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy coating has high hardness.
The high hardness of the coating resists abrasive wear.
The coating produces a 30% increase in wear resistance relative to uncoated Cu.
The wear-resistance improvement is measurable as reduced volume loss per unit sliding distance under a 10 N load.
The proposed coating-thickness boundary is 50 to 200 micrometers.
Wear-resistance enhancement may vary with deposition conditions, coating thickness, and testing parameters.
The HEA coating may introduce residual stresses that affect the Cu matrix.

contradictions.description: The oxide is located at the buried Cu/coating interface, but the mechanism assigns it prevention of the metal-to-metal contact responsible for sliding adhesive wear, which normally occurs at the coating/counterface wear surface. No pathway connecting the buried interfacial oxide to that tribological contact is stated.
